t: 3796. Find Maximum Value in a Constrained Sequence
o: Each position's value is capped by reachability from a[0] = 0: ignoring restrictions, a[i] ≤ Σ diff along the way. Restrictions add upper bounds at specific indices. The optimal sequence sets each a[i] to the tightest achievable bound, computed by a forward pass (cap[i] = min(cap[i-1] + diff[i-1], restriction[i])) followed by a backward pass (cap[i] = min(cap[i], cap[i+1] + diff[i])), because a restriction at a later index also limits earlier positions through the step constraint. The answer is max cap. diff[i] ≤ 10 keeps values bounded (~10⁶ scale), so plain ints suffice.
k: Two-pass constraint propagation (forward then backward) yields the pointwise-maximal feasible sequence, which maximizes the maximum.

a.i: Forward pass enforces a[i] ≤ a[i-1] + diff and restrictions; backward pass propagates later caps leftward since |a[i]-a[i+1]| ≤ diff implies a[i] ≤ a[i+1] + diff. The resulting caps are simultaneously achievable (set a[i] = cap[i]).
s: Initialize cap[i] = INF, apply restrictions cap[idx] = min(cap[idx], maxVal); cap[0] = 0.
a.t: O(n + R) — two linear passes plus reading restrictions

a.n: Approach 2: Sweep Between Sorted Restriction Points
a.i: Sort restrictions by index; between consecutive restricted points (and the anchors 0 and n-1), the reachable peak is bounded by both endpoints' caps plus accumulated diff. Compute each interval's max as min over approaching from either side; take the global max. Equivalent result, useful when n is huge but restrictions few.
s: Between consecutive points (i1,v1),(i2,v2): peak from left = v1 + Σdiff(i1..i2-1), from right = v2 + Σdiff back; interval max = min of the two (clamped ≥ 0 conceptually).
a.t: O(R log R) — sorting restriction points

w: Approach 1 is simpler and hard to get wrong; Approach 2 shines if n were astronomically large relative to R. Verify with sample 1 (answer 6 at index 5) and sample 2 (12 at the last index). Pitfall: forgetting the backward pass — restrictions late in the array constrain earlier peaks. Follow-up: what if diff values could differ per direction (asymmetric moves)?
